issue.title: Propagate directed hostility through orders and team knowledge
issue.body:
## Background

FTS-6A of #2496, Phase 12, `critical path`, `depends on #2558` (FTS-6E),
which must merge first; FTS-6F (#2561) is adjacent and may land before or
after. After FTS-6E an Attack order installs the attacker side's
hostility; nothing yet installs the target side's. This slice adds the
knowledge boundary D-13 and D-18 require: a damaged unit knows its
attacker locally, a same-group unit that can see the attack or death
witnesses it, and only a completed report by radio or in person installs
the reverse team-wide relation, once, in the report's group scope.

Verified on `master` `ca55a6fbc` (2026-09-07):

- **Local awareness is runtime-only and unit-local.** `Combat.Resolution`
  stamps `uiLastAttackerUid`/`uiLastAttackerAt` on every wound; both reset
  on load (`src/World/Save/Types.hs:969`); `unit.getLastAttacker` feeds the
  ten-second `incoming_hit` retaliation, the in-combat swap, and lash-out.
  FTS-5 (#2521) made retaliation relation-independent and installs nothing
  team-wide.
- **The notify pattern exists for one knowledge type.**
  `scripts/unit_ai_notify.lua` (260 lines, `notify_allies` goal) has a
  radio branch that broadcasts known water sources to every other
  radio-bearing unit whose definition is `acolyte` (`hasRadio` scans the
  inventory for a `radio` item; `isAcolyteUid` checks `defName`), and a
  walk branch with a rank-based split so two walkers never pick the same
  target. Only acolytes ship a radio (`data/units/acolyte.yaml:386`); nomads
  have none.
- **No engine-to-Lua combat event exists.** Nothing in `Combat.Resolution`
  or the Lua registrars calls into Lua on damage or death; AI modules poll
  `unit.getPose(uid) == "dead"` and `unit.getLastAttacker`. Perception is
  available as `unit.getVisibleTiles(uid)`, which the encounter AI already
  polls per tick for acquisition.
- **Group tags exist to scope a report.** FTS-6D (#2554) mints a roster
  team tag for controlled units and a per-location occupant group tag for
  location content; D-37 fixes report scope to those minted group tags,
  never a culture tag. FTS-6C (#2551) reads profiles and adds causes;
  FTS-6E's escalation lock engages the moment a reverse cause exists.
- **Coverage today** is indirect: `expedition_retrieval_probe` (a known
  flake) and the tutorial probes exercise the water notify path; no
  headless spec names `unit_ai_notify`.

Owner decisions 2026-09-07: incident knowledge and the pending report live
in the unit's Lua AI state and persist through `unit_ai_save.lua`; the
Haskell last-attacker fields keep their runtime-only retaliation role. A
witness is a same-group unit whose visible tiles contain the victim's tile
when the AI tick observes the damage or death.

## Requirements

1. Incident knowledge is a per-unit record in Lua AI state: the attacker
   unit, the attacker's group tag as read from its profile at that moment
   (roster team or occupant group; absent if it has none), the game time,
   and whether the incident has been reported. A damaged unit records the
   incident from `unit.getLastAttacker`; a same-group unit that observes a
   group member damaged or dead while the victim's tile is among its
   visible tiles records the same incident as a witness. A dead unit
   records and reports nothing.
2. A unit holding an unreported incident whose attacker group tag is
   present carries a pending report in its own group scope: with a radio,
   a broadcast to every other unit sharing its group tag that also carries
   a radio, after the existing broadcast delay; without one, the
   rank-split walk-and-notify to same-group units, reusing the `notify`
   phase state. Recipients are selected by shared group tag, never by
   definition name. Water-source notification keeps its current behavior
   and shares only the mechanics.
3. A completed report installs, once, the cause `<reporter's group tag> ->
   <attacker group tag>: hostile` under an owner derived from the incident
   so that repeated reports of the same incident are idempotent, and marks
   the incident reported on every informed unit. From that moment the
   informed group is triggered: uninvolved members acquire the attacker's
   group through FTS-5's current-hostility rule, and FTS-6E's lock holds
   both directions. An incident whose attacker has no group tag installs
   nothing and completes silently.
4. Local retaliation before a report installs nothing team-wide, and a
   report by one unit does not create knowledge in units it never reached:
   an uninformed same-group unit on another page keeps regarding the
   attacker by the base table until a report reaches it.
5. Incident records and pending-report phase persist through
   `unit_ai_save.lua` with the validator extended and its version bumped
   with a new tracked fixture; a load mid-walk or mid-broadcast resumes
   with the same next decision, and a load after the report carries the
   reported flag so nothing reports twice.
6. The Haskell last-attacker fields, the ten-second retaliation window,
   the in-combat swap, and lash-out targeting are unchanged.
7. No diplomacy UI, no reputation, no witness perception beyond the
   visible-tile rule, and no change to what an Attack order installs.

## Acceptance

A new headless spec whose top-level describe is exactly `Incident reports
and team knowledge` drives the real scripts and covers: an ordered attack
where the target group stays untriggered while the damaged unit retaliates
locally; an unwitnessed kill leaving no incident on any survivor; a witness
with the victim's tile visible recording the incident and one without it
not; a radio report installing the reverse cause exactly once across two
informed radio units; a walk report reaching a radio-less group member
before it acquires the attacker; the reverse cause locking FTS-6E's Hold;
an attacker with no group tag installing nothing; and save/load round
trips mid-walk, mid-broadcast, and post-report. The water notify path's
existing behavior is asserted unchanged in the same spec.

```bash
cabal build all
cabal build synarchy-test-headless
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Incident reports and team knowledge"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Attack order transaction"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "persistent ruin encounter AI"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "unit AI load reset"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua persistence components"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua faction model"'
python3 tools/save_compat_audit.py
python3 tools/test_save_compat_audit.py --only-reproducibility
python3 tools/test_lua_registration_audit.py && python3 tools/lua_registration_audit.py
python3 tools/lua_duplicate_function_audit.py
python3 tools/lua_module_budget.py
python3 tools/unicode_operator_audit.py
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only retaliation_swap_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only expedition_loop_probe
python3 tools/run_probes.py --only expedition_retrieval_probe
```

Expected: builds succeed; every spec group passes with the new group
non-empty; every audit exits zero with the bumped `unit_ai` fixture
tracked; the probes pass one at a time (re-run the retrieval probe once
before blaming the diff; it is a known flake on master).

## Out of scope

- Diplomacy resolution and grandfathered authorization: FTS-6F.
- General-purpose intelligence sharing, reputation, negotiation, any
  diplomacy UI, and multiplayer networking.
- Witnessing through anything other than the visible-tile rule; hearing,
  memory decay, or rumor.
- Removing the string verbs, `unit.getFaction`, or the adapter: FTS-7.

## Related

- Epic: #2496 (FTS-6A, Phase 12, critical path). Blocked by #2558
  (FTS-6E); #2551 and #2554 are its earlier prerequisites; #2561 (FTS-6F)
  is adjacent and independent of it.
- #538 (closed) split the notify module this slice generalizes; #916
  (closed) added the encounter AI whose members become the informed group;
  #1483 (closed) covers the mid-fight retaliation swap left unchanged.
- Design document (supporting detail, not required context):
  `docs/faction_tag_system_design.md`, sections "Local awareness and team
  knowledge", D-13, D-18, D-20, D-34, D-37.

## Automated cross-agent issue review

Reviewed against `master@36090b94a39a` by GPT-6-Astra (`gpt-6-astra` at `high`).

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Resolve requirements 3 and 4 explicitly: installing a hostile cause from the shared group tag changes the relation for every member carrying that tag, including unreached members on another page. Unit.Faction.Profile.relationFromTo (src/Unit/Faction/Profile.hs:433) evaluates matching tags and live causes without incident knowledge or page inputs; the declared FTS-6B contract wires that shared store into the relation authority.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Give each observed incident a stable identity shared by the victim and all witnesses, preserved through reporting and load. Distinguish separate victims and incidents, and ensure repeated polling cannot manufacture new incidents from an unchanged last-attacker stamp. Requirement 3 requires cross-reporter idempotency, while unit.getLastAttacker exposes only the latest attacker and timestamp and does not consume or expire them (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/Units/Combat.hs:423).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Require same-page qualification for witnessing and in-person delivery, including revalidation before transfer; matching tile coordinates alone must not establish visibility or proximity across pages. Add an equal-coordinates/different-pages regression case. This follows scripts/CLAUDE.md §Page qualification and the existing checks in scripts/unit_ai_encounter.lua.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Define successful communication as delivery to at least one eligible living recipient; a broadcast with no recipients must not install reverse hostility merely because its delay elapsed. Cover sender death during either pending phase. Requirements 1–3 and docs/faction_tag_system_design.md §Local awareness and team knowledge make living reporters and successful communication the escalation boundary.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Extend persistence coverage beyond the version bump: retain supported older unit_ai payloads with empty incident state, classify the new fields, and integrate entity references with the existing reference/reconciliation contract. Preserve historical incident identity and captured group tags if an attacker disappears, so reconciliation cannot change cause identity or erase a pending report. Grounding: scripts/unit_ai_save.lua, scripts/unit_ai_save_refs.lua, and docs/persistence_contract.md §2.

### Supporting context
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Reviewed snapshot 36090b94a39a773f65a7e9dc236efd971b38269d. The declared prerequisite chain was treated as delivered; absent prerequisite implementation was not counted as a blocker.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The existing notification implementation provides the stated broadcast delay and rank-split walking mechanics, with acolyte-specific water recipients (scripts/unit_ai_notify.lua). Generalizing incident delivery while preserving water behavior is a supported integration scope.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The design itself preserves both competing intentions: D-18 specifies a team-wide escalation relation, while §Local awareness and team knowledge requires explicit informed scope. D-37 selects a minted group tag but does not explain how unreached members sharing it retain a different relation (docs/faction_tag_system_design.md).

### Open decisions
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Does the first successful report make the entire minted group hostile, or must unreached members retain their previous relation? Requirements 3–4 specify both. If individual reach governs hostility, approve an explicit knowledge-aware relation/acquisition contract compatible with FTS-5/FTS-6B authority and FTS-6E's group escalation lock; the existing tag-only relation cannot express that distinction.

### Recommended disposition
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Revise requirements 3–4 around the owner's chosen scope and add a regression with informed and uninformed members sharing one group tag across two pages. If retaining group-wide relations, amend the unreached-member expectation; if retaining recipient-specific hostility, define the authority and escalation interaction before rerunning readiness review.

### Reviewer summaries
- **GPT-6-Astra — CHANGES REQUESTED:** The feature is actionable, but its group-wide hostility requirement conflicts with its per-recipient knowledge requirement. That policy choice needs resolution before implementation.
